why: I checked each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against the words of its expect line. Checks 1, 2 and 4 hold. They test clamping, a RangeError when lo > hi, and the npm test exit code with no failing tests. Check 3 breaks the criterion. Its script only counts a function as documented if a markdown heading matches `'^#+\\s*`?'+n+'\\s*\\('`, and its FAIL condition is "the script prints MISSING for any function". The expect line "README.md documents every function math.js exports" doesn't require headings in any format. A README that covers a function in a list, a table or a paragraph would still fail. This format rule is stricter than the words, but it sits in a PASS/FAIL condition instead of under Advisory. The Advisory section itself is fine, but Check 3's heading rule is enough to fail the whole output.
